text:
Predicates:
BredBack(x) ::: x is bred-back.
DomesticAnimal(x) ::: x is a domestic animal.
Resemble(x, y) ::: x resembles y.
Extinct(x) ::: x is extinct.
Premises:
∀x (BredBack(x) → DomesticAnimal(x)) ::: Breeding back is a form of artificial selection by the deliberate selective breeding of domestic animals.
BredBack(heckCattle) ∧ Resemble(heckCattle, aurochs) ∧ Year(heckCattle, 1920s) ::: Heck cattle were bred-back in the 1920s to resemble the aurochs. [BG]
Animals(heckCattle) ::: Heck cattle are animals. [BG]
Animals(aurochs) ::: Aurochs are animals. [BG]
∃x (BredBack(x) ∧ Resemble(x, extinctAnimal)) ::: Some animals to be bred-back resemble animals that are extinct.
Conclusion:
Extinct(aurochs) ::: Aurochs are extinct.
